inputs.note: Needs the locate step (merged to main with D24). D24 is the authoritative policy and this case asserts it rather than restating it (D41). The exclusion is a property of the VALUE CLASS, not of one field: app/extraction/locate.py EXACT_ONLY_VALUE_CLASSES = {NUMERIC, UNIT, DATE, FLAG}. Drive locate() with a candidate one character off in each of the four classes — `111` for a drawn `11.1`, `mg/dt` for `mg/dL`, `2026-03-02` for `2026-08-02`, `H` for `N` — on a scanned page, under every FuzzyMode including ALWAYS, since D24 says the policy is not a default that ALWAYS can lift. W2-C7 asserts the numeric case against one fixture; this asserts it over the whole class set and the tier order, which is where it would be re-introduced.

expected: On a scanned page, a one-character-off value in any of the four exact-only classes is NOT located by any tier — not exact, not numeric, not number_only, and not fuzzy even with FuzzyMode.ALWAYS. It comes back not_located and is disclosed as unsupported.
guards_against: D24 quietly relaxed by a later branch. agent/tests/test_locate_measurement.py holds the same policy against the locate module and moves with the branch that owns it; this case is the copy in a gated directory, which an implementation session cannot weaken. A near miss changes the meaning in all four classes: a misread number, a unit read as a neighbouring column's, a collection date one digit out, a flag `N` read as `H`. In every one the damage is not the misread but the bbox that follows it — a located fact with a citation a reviewer can click and confirm, built on a value that is not on the page.
